user_scenario: You are Ruth Ann Sizemore, in your sixties, who keeps the books for the family farm on Pleasant Run Road and has been a Cedar Fork member since the eighties. You are friendly, organized and a little talkative, and you like to know where each dollar goes. Back in 2023 you took over the old farmhouse and put down a security deposit on the house account; you remember it as six hundred forty dollars, paid in three parts. In January your husband had the grain dryer moved off the house meter onto the new bin meter, and the house bills have dropped a lot since. You open by saying something like: "I'd like our deposit back on the house account, or whatever part of it you're allowed to give back now that the dryer's off that meter. And I want it as a check mailed to us, not a credit on the bill." When asked who you are, you give your name, Ruth Ann Sizemore, and the phone number on the account, 2705554318. If the agent needs to verify you, you give your membership number, 0447213, and the last four of your Social Security number, 4527. You know the house is at 6215 Pleasant Run Road and that the bin site has its own meter, but you do not know any account numbers by heart. If the agent explains that the whole deposit cannot come back because of some late payments, you sigh that the checks were late a few times when money was tight before harvest, and say you will take whatever part can come back. You never offer any amount, rate or rule yourself, and you do not ask about interest. When the agent hands the refund over to you to confirm, you confirm the check for the amount the agent tells you, to the mailing address on file. Once the agent tells you the refund check has been set up, you thank them, mention you will watch the mailbox, and end the call.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (security_deposit_lifecycle)
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [4,6,4]. Assigned: year-end accrual (deposit_ext_year_end_interest) 4; refund-date accrual (deposit_ext_refund_date_interest) 4; recalculation refund (deposit_ext_recalculation_refund, root) 6.
[Scope] Occupied by task 0: deposit_assess (reinstatement, reconnection) and deposit_payment with tools assess_reinstated_deposit_c3ac4854, assess_reconnection_deposit_9009d8a2, pay_reinstated_deposit_installment_114bda0d. Task 1 claims the untouched interest and refund families: deposit_interest_accrual (year-end and refund-date, two distinct base clauses) and deposit_refund by check at the member's request. Disjoint from task 0 in policies, tools and write operations; together the two tasks cover all six extended policies.
[Why a good test] The member asks for her deposit back (or the part that can come back) as a check. The agent must see that the good-payment review fails (three late charges in the twelve-month window against an allowance of two), find the recalculation path, compute a six-factor recalculated requirement over the right window, and before refunding bring the interest current: the refund waits on a refund-date accrual, which waits on the missing 2025 December 31 accrual. Each accrual has its own supplement/day rules. Nothing names interest in the request.
[Problem-tree card] Chain. Edge 1: recalculation refund -> refund-date accrual, kind value_input, gate unpaid_interest, form state, sentence 'The recalculation refund is not made until the deposit ledger carries an interest accrual whose period ends on the refund date.' (negated; 'not ... until'; state = an accrual entry ending on the refund date; no tool/id/code token; hard). Only the refund-date accrual policy writes such an entry. False at opening: ledger's latest accrual ends 2024-12-31; deposit_accounts.690944d6-6fe3-4eba-977b-8ec03d84abfd.accrued_interest=0.0. Edge 2: refund-date accrual -> year-end accrual, kind value_input, gate base_days, form state, sentence 'The refund-date accrual is worked out only after the deposit ledger carries a December 31 accrual for every earlier calendar year in which cash was held.' (affirmative; 'only after'). Only the year-end accrual policy writes a December 31 accrual. False at opening: cash held since 2023-06-26 but no 2025 accrual. Order: year-end accrual, refund-date accrual, refund (no free pair). Deletion runs: skip refund-date accrual -> refund 389.54 instead of 399.39; skip year-end accrual -> refund-date accrual recomputes to 22.60 (594 days) instead of 9.85 and the replayed refund is 384.85. user_scenario mentions no accrual; tools validate nothing.
[Base-invariant card] deposit_interest_accrual (steps 11, 13): deposit_evt_interest.interest_on_cash_held - record held. deposit_refund (step 15): deposit_evt_refund.held_long_enough - anchor paid_in_full_date 2023-06-26, refund_good_payment_months 12 for Farm Service, calendar months to the same day number, inclusive: boundary 2024-06-26, satisfied at 2026-10-06; refund_only_from_held - status held; deposit_evt_cancellation - scope only (energized account).
